documented_sections.heading: FastAPI CLI { #fastapi-cli }

independent_workflow_mappings.scope_note: Partial: the selected process cases capture the top-level help output and one successful default ``fastapi dev`` server request. They do not cover every subcommand, project-management commands, all entrypoint discovery rules, reload output, deployment, or the complete CLI terminal transcript.

documented_sections.review_rationale: Pinned FastAPI 0.141.1 docs/en/docs/fastapi-cli.md:1-7 introduces the optional command-line program and its ``fastapi dev`` usage. Its ``standard`` extra requires ``fastapi-cli[standard] >=0.0.32`` and exposes ``fastapi = fastapi.cli:main`` (../fastapi/pyproject.toml:59-62, 119-120); the standard oracle pins fastapi-cli 0.0.32 (metadata.yaml:102). FastAPI's entrypoint delegates to that optional package (../fastapi/fastapi/cli.py:1-13). Both selected cases in ``fastapi-cli-documented-process-v2.yaml`` cite this exact docs page as ``upstream_documentation``; they observe process output for root help and process completion plus one HTTP response for the dev app.

documented_sections.heading: Configure the app `entrypoint` in `pyproject.toml` { #configure-the-app-entrypoint-in-pyproject-toml }

independent_workflow_mappings.scope_note: One isolated `fastapi dev` case reads `[tool.fastapi] entrypoint = "backend.main:app"`, imports that app, and serves one GET `/probe` request. The selectors cover process completion and that HTTP response. The nested command-option section, invalid configuration, explicit-entrypoint precedence, auto-discovery, terminal output, and reload behavior are outside this mapping.

documented_sections.review_rationale: FastAPI 0.157.0's optional `standard` extra requires `fastapi-cli[standard] >=0.0.32` (../fastapi/pyproject.toml:59-61), and its console script is `fastapi = fastapi.cli:main` (../fastapi/pyproject.toml:119-120). The standard oracle pins fastapi-cli 0.0.32 (metadata.yaml:100-104). The separately packaged fastapi-cli implements project entrypoint discovery, so this is the pinned FastAPI optional CLI surface rather than core ASGI behavior. Starlette 1.6.0 owns generic ASGI and HTTP transport behavior for the selected probe.

documented_sections.heading: `fastapi dev` with path or with `--entrypoint` CLI option { #fastapi-dev-with-path-or-with-entrypoint-cli-option }

independent_workflow_mappings.scope_note: Partial: one isolated process passes ``main.py`` as the path and one passes a module-qualified app through ``--entrypoint``; both make one GET request to the selected app and observe process exit plus HTTP status/body. The cases do not compare precedence, invalid paths, the ``pyproject.toml`` entrypoint, or CLI output.

documented_sections.review_rationale: Pinned FastAPI 0.141.1 docs/en/docs/fastapi-cli.md:98-115 documents the path argument, ``--entrypoint``, and the recommendation to configure the entrypoint in ``pyproject.toml``. The selected ``dev-path-preserves-environment`` and ``dev-explicit-entrypoint`` cases in ``fastapi-cli-documented-process-v2.yaml`` use those two command forms and each carries the exact page as ``upstream_documentation`` evidence. The pin is FastAPI 0.141.1's optional ``fastapi-cli[standard] >=0.0.32`` integration (../fastapi/pyproject.toml:59-62; metadata.yaml:102); the cases sample only the selected server response and process exit.

documented_sections.heading: `fastapi dev` { #fastapi-dev }

independent_workflow_mappings.scope_note: Partial: one default ``fastapi dev`` process exposes the inserted ``FASTAPI_ENV=development`` value through its route response, and one process preserves a pre-existing ``FASTAPI_ENV=staging`` value. Both observe process exit and HTTP status/body. They do not observe reload output, filesystem watching, or the default loopback bind address.

documented_sections.review_rationale: Pinned FastAPI 0.141.1 docs/en/docs/fastapi-cli.md:116-125 documents the development command, auto-reload, loopback address, and ``FASTAPI_ENV`` default/preservation rules. The selected process cases use the same pinned optional CLI workflow and exact page-level ``upstream_documentation`` evidence; the route input returns the environment value so the chosen HTTP body selector observes only that limited behavior. FastAPI exposes the pinned CLI through ``fastapi-cli[standard]`` (../fastapi/pyproject.toml:59-62, 119-120; ../fastapi/fastapi/cli.py:1-13), while this mapping makes no claim about reload or bind-address results.

documented_sections.heading: `fastapi run` { #fastapi-run }

independent_workflow_mappings.scope_note: Partial: one ``fastapi run`` invocation auto-discovers the app and serves a single GET request; the process exit and response status/body are selected. The case explicitly sets host to 127.0.0.1, so this mapping does not establish the documented default bind address, reload setting, proxy setup, or a full production deployment.

documented_sections.review_rationale: Pinned FastAPI 0.141.1 docs/en/docs/fastapi-cli.md:126-138 describes ``fastapi run`` as the production-mode command and links deployment guidance. The selected ``fastapi.cli.process.run-auto-discovery-no-path`` case in ``fastapi-cli-documented-process-v2.yaml`` invokes that command, sends one request, and carries this exact page as ``upstream_documentation`` evidence. FastAPI 0.141.1 exposes this optional integration through its pinned fastapi-cli standard extra (../fastapi/pyproject.toml:59-62, 119-120; metadata.yaml:102); the case's explicit host override is why no default production bind claim is made.

FastAPI wraps generator dependencies as context managers and enters them on the selected exit stack (`../fastapi/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py:566-574,662-672`); its routing stacks surround response creation and sending (`../fastapi/fastapi/routing.py:137-158`).

A follow-up request observes the cleanup trace. The generic 500 response and application-error transport are Starlette behavior; this input uses them to expose FastAPI's dependency teardown path and does not sample exception translation or suppression.

documented_sections.review_rationale: The tutorial's `tutorial007` dependency wraps `yield` in `try/finally` (`../fastapi/docs_src/dependencies/tutorial007_py310.py:3-6`). FastAPI enters the generator as a context manager (`../fastapi/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py:566-574`) and exits its request stack around response dispatch (`../fastapi/fastapi/routing.py:137-158`), returning the endpoint exception through teardown. Starlette 1.6.0 owns the generic unhandled-error response.

reviewed_module_mapping.contract_gate: Partial source review. The source tests parameterize both legacy default-value declarations and typing.Annotated declarations. The independent workload includes both forms for the reviewed file/form endpoints, but uses new paths and handlers. The recipes send concrete ASGI bodies directly. They do not exercise HTTPX or TestClient's multipart encoding, response wrapper, or transport behavior; those generic behaviors remain Starlette 1.6.0/Starlette-RS-owned. HTTP response bytes are selected because the current workflow contract supports them. This is stricter than upstream response.json() assertions and can distinguish JSON encoding or whitespace. The OpenAPI case observes the whole document for the independent combined workload. It does not claim literal equality with each tutorial app's operation IDs, titles, route set, or inline snapshot. All recipe requests run with the pinned python-multipart profile. They do not establish behavior when the optional parser is absent or when an incorrectly named multipart distribution is installed. FastAPI 0.157.0 requires Python >=3.10. The selected oracle is CPython 3.12.13; no compatibility claim is made below 3.10 or for another Python minor runtime. Pydantic model validation is exercised for form models, including extra=forbid. The complete Pydantic API, arbitrary custom validators, and pydantic-core internals are outside this test slice. This review performs only static source, link, and recipe-schema checks. No oracle/target parity run or compatibility pass is claimed.
reviewed_module_mapping.rationale: Required bytes and UploadFile parameters. FastAPI owns the Rust-side parameter/body and validation integration. Starlette 1.6.0, implemented by Starlette-RS, owns generic request parsing, UploadFile, responses, and TestClient. Pydantic owns model validation/schema behavior where these cases use form models.
reviewed_module_mapping.stimulus_notes: Input-only recipes and independent workloads are declared by each workflow link. Every test function maps to a case and selectors. Fixture functions map to the module's full set of reviewed test cases as setup provenance.
